report.summary: Audit found one severe docstring-implementation gap in _mode() where review-only tasks get mode 'write' for low-risk ollama/codex, contradicting its own docstring. Also, routing allows high-risk review-only tasks to go to external DeepSeek, and concurrent index reads could yield corrupted verdicts.

risks.description: _mode() docstring says review-only is advisory for Ollama/Codex, but code returns 'write' when risk=='low', regardless of review_only. This misinforms downstream about write capability.
risks.trigger: Call select_provider with objective containing 'review', risk='low', agent external_ok=True, provider='ollama' available.

risks.description: High-risk review-only tasks are not forced to Claude; they can reach branch 4 and be routed to DeepSeek (external). The policy explicitly forces high-risk *writes* to Claude but not reviews.
risks.trigger: Call select_provider with risk='high' (maybe due to reachability), review_only=True, data not sensitive, deepseek available.

risks.description: Concurrent index rebuild during routing decision can lead to reading a corrupt or empty index. The code sets escalate=False on empty index unless a source file is missing, potentially under-escalating.
risks.trigger: Run routing while another process is rebuilding the cached index; a partially written file is read.

handoff.suggestion: Fix _mode() to return 'advisory' for review_only tasks for ollama/codex, matching docstring. Consider adding explicit check for high-risk review-only tasks to stay on Claude when data not sensitive. Add file locking or atomic read mechanism for index access.
